summary: Cross-cutting codes, standards and federal tax rules that shape BTM C&I LFP storage sizing in MA, CT, NYC, IL, TX and CA. Fire code (IFC 2021/2024 Section 1207, NFPA 855-2023) is the dominant sizing constraint: all four SKUs exceed the 50 kWh prescriptive unit limit and rely on UL 9540A/large-scale fire test acceptance, and the 600 kWh Li-ion MAQ allows only one 418 or 600 kWh unit (or 3-4 smaller units) per group near exposures without an HMA + LSFT; outdoor pads need 10 ft from lot lines/buildings/egress (3 ft with barriers/testing). Electrically, 200 kW units at 208 V rarely fit the NEC 705.12 120% rule, so 480 V service, supply-side taps or listed PCS current limiting are typical, and charging load must fit service headroom (125% continuous, NEC 220.87). Non-export interconnection (32R/32F relays or UL 1741 CRD PCS) caps useful discharge at site minimum load, especially on secondary networks. Federally, OBBBA preserved the 48E storage ITC at 30% (PWA or <1 MW AC) through construction start in 2033 (+10 pp adders possible), but FEOC material-assistance thresholds (55% in 2026 rising to 75%) put China-sourced LFP cabinets' ITC at risk; 100% bonus depreciation is restored.

programs.name: Section 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit - energy storage technology (post-OBBBA)
programs.status_notes: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) left storage on the full 48E schedule: full credit for construction beginning by 2033-12-31; 75% for BOC in 2034; 50% for BOC in 2035; 0% for BOC 2036+. Wind/solar were cut back; storage was not. Beginning of construction for storage still via physical work test or 5% safe harbor (Notice 2025-42 limits applied to wind/solar only and that Notice was vacated by D.D.C. on 2026-06-06). Prohibited-foreign-entity (FEOC) material-assistance rules apply to storage beginning construction after 2025-12-31.

eligibility.other: Electrical energy storage technology >=5 kWh (standalone OK). Must satisfy PWA for the 30% rate unless max net output <1 MW AC (One Megawatt Exception; nameplate AC; aggregated across facilities with integrated operations). Must meet MACR thresholds (no material assistance from prohibited foreign entities) for BOC after 2025; taxpayer cannot be a specified foreign entity / foreign-influenced entity.

valuation.cap: None, but depreciable basis reduced by 50% of credit (IRC 50(c)(3))

tiers.conditions: +10 pp (or +2 pp if base 6%); 100% US steel/iron for structural components + manufactured-products adjusted percentage (50% BOC 2026, 55% BOC after 2026 per OBBBA alignment)

tiers.conditions: +10 pp (or +2 pp if base 6%) if sited in a statistical area/brownfield/coal-closure energy community

valuation.notes: Model: ITC = 0.30 x eligible basis (+0.10 domestic content, +0.10 energy community where verified). Depreciable basis = cost - 0.5 x ITC. Transferable under IRC 6418 (cash at a discount); 5-yr recapture period. Low-income-community bonus (48E(h)) allocations are for solar/wind and generally not available to standalone storage (verify).

programs.vpp_relevance: Per-site BTM projects are small; aggregation into a VPP does not by itself create 'integrated operations' for the 1 MW test, but multiple cabinets at one site do aggregate.

programs.name: Prohibited Foreign Entity (FEOC) material-assistance cost ratio (MACR) - energy storage
programs.status_notes: Applies to 45Y/48E facilities and energy storage technology beginning construction after 2025-12-31. Notice 2026-15 (released 2026-02-12) gives interim MACR guidance and three interim safe harbors (use of domestic-content tables and supplier certifications) usable until 60 days after forthcoming safe-harbor tables are published. Proposed regs pending.

eligibility.other: MACR = (total direct costs of manufactured products/components - PFE-sourced direct costs) / total direct costs; must be >= threshold for BOC year.

valuation.notes: Failing MACR = loss of the entire 48E credit (all-or-nothing). Chinese-made LFP cells/modules/PCS are typically PFE-sourced; with cells ~35-45% of system cost (per vendor cost breakdowns) a China-cell cabinet is at high risk of failing 55%+ thresholds. Obtain supplier MACR certifications per Notice 2026-15 before procurement.

programs.vpp_relevance: Supply-chain decision applies fleet-wide; a non-compliant SKU removes ITC from every site.

site_constraints.title: Li-ion ESS regulated at >=20 kWh (IFC 2021/2024 Table 1207.1.1; NFPA 855-2023)
site_constraints.rule: IFC Section 1207 and NFPA 855 apply to lithium-ion ESS with aggregate stored energy at or above 20 kWh. Below that, ESS chapter rules (spacing, MAQ, HMA, detection) do not apply.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Every SKU (150-600 kWh) is a fully regulated ESS. No 'small system' path exists for any product.
site_constraints.applies_to: All jurisdictions adopting IFC 2018+ or NFPA 855 (MA, CT, NYC, IL, TX, CA all base fire codes on IFC or NFPA 1/855; local amendments vary - NYC FC 608 and CA CFC have their own amendments)

site_constraints.title: Fire-code construction/operational permit required for ESS above Table 1207.1.1 thresholds
site_constraints.rule: IFC requires construction and operational permits for stationary ESS regulated by Section 1207 (i.e., Li-ion >=20 kWh), in addition to the electrical/building permit. Expect plan review of UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A report, HMA (if triggered), emergency response plan and commissioning plan.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: All SKUs need a fire permit; the permit package (9540A, HMA, ERP) is the long pole on schedule, not the electrical permit.
site_constraints.applies_to: IFC-adopting jurisdictions; local amendments (e.g., NYC FDNY Certificate of Approval, CA CFC) may add steps

site_constraints.title: Electrochemical ESS units/groups limited to 50 kWh unless approved via large-scale fire testing (IFC 1207.5.1; NFPA 855-2023)
site_constraints.rule: Electrochemical ESS shall be segregated into groups not exceeding 50 kWh, each group separated >=3 ft from other groups and walls. Where approved by the fire code official, larger capacities or smaller separations are allowed based on large-scale fire testing (IFC 2021 1207.1.5; UL 9540A report). Applies indoors and to outdoor installations near exposures; not to remote outdoor installations (>100 ft from exposures).

threshold.scope: per unit or group (without LSFT approval)

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: ALL four SKUs exceed 50 kWh per cabinet, so every installation depends on the AHJ accepting the vendor's UL 9540A (cell/module/unit; Ed. 6 adds large-scale fire test) report as justification. Without an acceptable 9540A/LSFT report the products are not prescriptively code-compliant anywhere that enforces this section.

site_constraints.title: 3 ft separation between ESS units/groups and from walls (reducible with 9540A data)
site_constraints.rule: ESS units/groups must be separated by a minimum of 3 ft (914 mm) from each other and from walls, unless smaller distances are documented adequate by UL 9540A/large-scale fire and explosion testing and approved.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Stacking N cabinets needs ~3 ft between each plus front/rear service clearances (NEC 110.26 working space in front of doors). Many vendor 9540A reports justify side-by-side or 6-12 in spacing - get the vendor's tested spacing in writing; it drives pad footprint.

site_constraints.title: Li-ion maximum allowable quantity 600 kWh per fire area (IFC 1207.5.2 / Table 1207.5; NFPA 855-2023)
site_constraints.rule: Rooms/areas (and, per Mayfield's reading of IFC Table 1207.8, outdoor installations near exposures) containing Li-ion ESS shall not exceed 600 kWh aggregate. Exceeding it requires fire code official approval based on a Hazard Mitigation Analysis (1207.1.6) and large-scale fire testing (1207.1.7). Not applicable to dedicated-use buildings or remote outdoor installations.

threshold.scope: per fire area / outdoor group near exposures

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Units per prescriptive group: 30/150 -> 4 units (600 kWh); 65/200 -> 3 units (600); 200/418 -> 1 unit (2 = 836 kWh exceeds); 200/600 -> 1 unit (exactly at limit). Larger clusters need HMA + LSFT approval, or split into separate groups separated per AHJ, or a remote outdoor location (>100 ft).

sku_impact.200kW/600kWh: max 1 per group (at limit); 2+ needs HMA+LSFT

site_constraints.applies_to: IFC 2021/2024 and NFPA 855-2023 jurisdictions. NFPA 855-2026 reportedly drops the separate max-stored-energy cap in favor of default HMA (low-confidence secondary source) - verify against adopted edition.

site_constraints.title: Outdoor ESS 10 ft from lot lines, buildings, public ways, combustibles (IFC 1207.8.3); 3 ft with exceptions
site_constraints.rule: Outdoor ESS near exposures must be >=10 ft from lot lines, public ways, buildings, stored combustibles, hazardous materials and other exposures. Exceptions reduce building clearance to 3 ft: (1) 1-hour free-standing exterior fire barrier extending 5 ft above and 5 ft beyond the ESS; other exceptions incl. approved large-scale fire testing (fire code official may approve smaller distances/larger capacities).
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Small retail parcels and zero-lot-line urban sites often cannot fit 10 ft clearance; budget for a 1-hr barrier wall or rely on the vendor LSFT report. Pad location is frequently the binding constraint, not electrical capacity.
site_constraints.applies_to: IFC 2021/2024 jurisdictions; NFPA 855 has similar outdoor provisions

site_constraints.title: Outdoor/garage ESS >=10 ft from means of egress (IFC 2024 1207.5.8)
site_constraints.rule: ESS outdoors and in open parking garages must be separated from any means of egress by a distance set by the fire code official, but not less than 10 ft.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Keep pads away from exit doors, exit discharge paths and egress stairs; also keep away from HVAC/air intakes and operable openings (practice, not a fixed code number).
site_constraints.applies_to: Jurisdictions on IFC 2024 (or with equivalent amendments)

site_constraints.title: Remote outdoor installation = >100 ft from buildings, lot lines, public ways, exposures (IFC 1207.8.1)
site_constraints.rule: ESS located more than 100 ft from buildings, lot lines, public ways, stored combustibles, hazardous materials, high-piled stock and other exposure hazards are 'remote' and are exempt from size/separation and MAQ limits.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Only large-campus C&I sites (industrial yards, big-box parking fields) can reach 100 ft; there, multiple 200/600 units can be clustered without the 600 kWh MAQ - at the cost of long AC cable runs (voltage drop, trenching).

site_constraints.title: Rooftop ESS: 10 ft from exposures and from fire-service access point; 5 ft service walkways; stair access (IFC 1207.9)
site_constraints.rule: Rooftop (and open garage) ESS must be >=10 ft from exposures; rooftop systems must be >=10 ft from the rooftop fire service access point, have >=5 ft wide service walkways from roof access to the system, and stair access (interior bulkhead or exterior stair). Electrochemical ESS also have floor-elevation limits (not more than 75 ft above fire department vehicle access / 30 ft below exit discharge) - verify in adopted code.

threshold.scope: rooftop ESS to exposures/fire access point

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Rooftop placement of 418-600 kWh outdoor cabinets is rarely practical: structural load, crane lift, 10 ft clearances and stair-access requirements. Treat rooftop as exception-only (NYC sites may have no ground space - FDNY has its own rooftop rules).

site_constraints.title: Open parking garage ESS: 10 ft from exposures and egress; vehicle impact protection (IFC 1207.9)
site_constraints.rule: ESS in open parking garages follow the special-installation rules: >=10 ft separation from exposures and >=10 ft from means of egress; impact protection where subject to vehicle damage. Enclosed garages are treated as indoor installations (600 kWh MAQ, sprinklers, detection, explosion control).
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Retail sites with structured parking can host cabinets on open decks only with bollards, 10 ft clearances and usually 9540A-justified spacing; expect AHJ scrutiny and insurer pushback.

site_constraints.title: ESS must be listed to UL 9540 (3rd ed. 2023); UL 9540A test report required for large-scale-fire-test based approvals
site_constraints.rule: IFC 1207 / NFPA 855 / NEC 706.5 require ESS listed to UL 9540. UL 9540 3rd edition (published 2023-06-28, effective Sept 2024) aligned capacity/separation limits with NFPA 855 and added explosion control, external warning communication, noise and liquid-coolant requirements. UL 9540A is a test method (not a listing) whose report is used to justify units >50 kWh, reduced spacing and exceeding MAQ. UL 9540A 6th edition (published 2026-03-13; effective 2027-01-01) integrates a large-scale fire test as the 4th level and drops the unit-level test for non-residential BESS.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Procurement gate: require UL 9540 (3rd ed.) listing of the complete cabinet incl. PCS, plus 9540A report (and ideally LSFT per NFPA 855-2026 Annex G.11 / UL 9540A Ed. 6). Products tested to older editions may face AHJ questions after 2027-01-01.

site_constraints.title: NFPA 855-2026 edition published; adoption lagging; HMA becomes default
site_constraints.rule: NFPA 855 2026 edition is published (on sale at NFPA/ICC). Key changes: HMA becomes default for most BESS (previously only when thresholds exceeded); large-scale fire testing emphasized (Annex G.11); technologies listed individually with own thresholds; updated Qualified Person definition; EPSS/SEPSS section. Secondary sources report removal of the separate max-stored-energy cap (unverified). Most states still enforce IFC 2021/2024 + NFPA 855-2020/2023 until they adopt.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Where 2026 is adopted, expect an HMA even for a single cabinet; budget ~engineering cost and time per site. The 600 kWh cap may be replaced by HMA/LSFT-driven limits.
site_constraints.applies_to: Jurisdictions adopting NFPA 855-2026 (check state fire code adoption: MA 527 CMR 1 (NFPA 1), CT State Fire Safety Code, NYC FC, IL OSFM, TX local, CA CFC)

site_constraints.title: Inverter/PCS certification: UL 1741 SB (IEEE 1547-2018 / IEEE 1547.1-2020) grid support
site_constraints.rule: Utilities in target states require inverter-based DER, including storage, to be certified UL 1741 SB (3rd ed., Sept 2021) as Grid Support Utility Interactive, demonstrating IEEE 1547-2018 conformance per IEEE 1547.1-2020, with settings per the utility/state Source Requirements Document (e.g., MA TSRG SRD, ISO-NE SRD). CA Rule 21 and NY SIR require UL 1741 SB for new projects.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: No sizing cap, but verify each SKU's PCS has UL 1741 SB certificate and can load the state SRD settings profile; non-SB legacy inverters (UL 1741 SA) will be rejected.
site_constraints.applies_to: MA, CT, NY, IL, CA (TX/ERCOT distribution utilities increasingly require IEEE 1547-2018 - verify per utility)

site_constraints.title: Export control via UL 1741 CRD for Power Control Systems (PCS); OLRT <=30 s typical, some utilities require <=2 s
site_constraints.rule: A PCS certified to the UL 1741 Certification Requirement Decision (CRD) for PCS (being transitioned to UL 3141) can limit export (modes: unrestricted, export-only, import-only, no-exchange). IREC/BATRIES model rules: certified PCS with maximum open-loop response time <=30 s to limit inadvertent export; some utility rules (e.g., CA Rule 21 limited-export) specify OLRT <=2 s. PCS export/import settings are recognized in screens to treat the DER at its controlled export rather than nameplate.

threshold.scope: PCS open-loop response time, seconds (model default; some utilities 2 s)

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Lets a site with large BESS kW pass hosting-capacity screens as non-export. Confirm the PCS listing covers the vendor's site controller + meter CT combination, and the import-only mode (to prove charging only from grid where needed).

site_constraints.title: Non-export via reverse power relay (ANSI 32R): default 0.1% of service transformer rating, <=2.0 s
site_constraints.rule: Model (IREC/BATRIES) non-export option: utility-grade reverse-power relay (32R) at the PCC set to 0.1% (export) of the service transformer nameplate with max 2.0 s time delay. Utility-specific settings vary.

threshold.scope: export pickup as fraction of service transformer kVA; delay <=2.0 s

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Relay trip disconnects the BESS: design the EMS to hold a small import margin so the relay never trips (nuisance trips = lost demand-charge savings).
site_constraints.applies_to: Utility-specific; common in NY SIR, MA/CT interconnection practice

site_constraints.title: Minimum import relay (ANSI 32F/under-power): default 5% of DER nameplate import, <=2.0 s
site_constraints.rule: Model minimum-import protective function: utility-grade relay set to 5% (import) of the DER's total nameplate rating with max 2.0 s delay. Network-grid utilities often require minimum import relays at higher margins.

threshold.scope: required import as fraction of DER nameplate kW; delay <=2.0 s

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Usable discharge kW = site load - min import margin. At low-load hours (nights, weekends) a 200 kW unit may only be able to discharge a fraction of rated power. Size kW to the site's minimum load during the target window, not the peak.

site_constraints.title: Secondary (spot/area) networks: DER must never cause export into the network; protectors' 32 function trips on reverse flow
site_constraints.rule: Network protectors open on reverse power flow from the low-voltage bus. Utilities (e.g., Con Edison) require that DER on grid/spot networks never activate network protector reverse-power elements, i.e., an effective requirement of no export from the secondary network to primary, typically enforced with minimum import relays and import margins. Some utilities cap DER as a % of minimum network load.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Downtown Boston, Manhattan/NYC, Chicago Loop, downtown CA cities: battery must be strictly non-export with min-import margin; discharge kW capped by the site's (and sometimes the network's) minimum load. Study timelines are longer and protection upgrades possible.
site_constraints.applies_to: Network-served sites (Con Edison, Eversource Boston, ComEd Loop, PG&E SF/Oakland, SCE/others)

site_constraints.title: NEC 2023 705.12(B)(2) load-side busbar '120% rule'
site_constraints.rule: Load-side connection, backfed breaker at the opposite end from the main: 1.25 x (sum of inverter rated output currents) + (rating of OCPD protecting the busbar) <= 1.20 x busbar rating. (Was 705.12(B)(3)(2) in NEC 2020.) Other 705.12(B) options: 100% rule (sum of 125% source current + main OCPD <= busbar), center-fed, feeder-tap rules, or PCS-limited current (705.13).
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Per-unit inverter current (kW/(sqrt3*V), 125% in parentheses): 30 kW @208V 83.3 A (104.1 A), @480V 36.1 A (45.1 A); 65 kW @208V 180.4 A (225.5 A), @480V 78.2 A (97.7 A); 200 kW @208V 555.1 A (693.9 A), @480V 240.6 A (300.7 A). Example: 2000 A switchboard with 2000 A main allows 0.2*2000 = 400 A of 125% current = 320 A inverter = ~266 kW at 480 V (~115 kW at 208 V). 200 kW units at 208 V almost never fit load-side - use 480 V service, supply-side tap, or PCS. Use the PCS nameplate max continuous current (kVA-based), not kW.
site_constraints.applies_to: All target states (NEC 2020/2023 adopted variously; CA CEC 2022 = NEC 2020 basis)

sources.title: Mayfield - Code Corner: 2020 NEC 705.12(B)(3)(1) and (2)

site_constraints.title: NEC 705.11 supply-side (line-side) connection
site_constraints.rule: Connection between the utility meter and the service disconnect. The sum of power-source continuous current output ratings on a service (other than those controlled per 705.13) shall not exceed the ampacity of the service conductors; tap conductors sized for 125% of source output, with disconnect/OCPD per 705.11 and 230.82. Utility approval of the tap location (CT cabinet, meter socket, switchgear) is often required.

threshold.scope: sum of source outputs <= service conductor ampacity

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Main path for 200 kW units when switchboard busbars fail the 120% rule. Caps aggregate BESS output at the service conductor ampacity (e.g., 1600 A service ~1,330 kW @480 V). Tapping utility-owned or sealed sections may need utility outage and approval.

site_constraints.title: NEC 705.13 PCS/EMS current limiting to busbar/conductor ampacity
site_constraints.rule: A listed PCS (2023 NEC frames it as an EMS per 750.30, with PCS as a type of EMS; 2026 NEC 705.13 again titled Power Control Systems) may limit current/loading on busbars and conductors. The sum of PCS-controlled currents plus monitored currents from other sources shall not exceed busbar/conductor ampacity; where connected to an OCPD protecting unmonitored busbar/conductor, the PCS setting must be within that OCPD rating. PCS settings (not nameplate) can be used in 705.12 calculations.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Allows several cabinets on a busbar that fails the 120% rule by capping discharge current; also allows limiting charging import to protect service headroom. Requires PCS listing (UL 1741 CRD PCS / UL 3141) and AHJ acceptance.

site_constraints.title: NEC 2023 Article 706 key items (ESS >1 kWh)
site_constraints.rule: 706 applies to ESS >1 kWh. Key items: ESS must be listed (UL 9540); 706.7 commissioning at installation and maintenance with written records for other than 1-2 family dwellings; 706.15 disconnecting means - readily accessible, within the ESS or within sight and within 10 ft, or lockable open where not within sight (with remote-control/notification provisions); circuit conductors and OCPD sized from the ESS maximum rated (charge/discharge) current at 125% (continuous); labeling/marking; Art. 480 for batteries; NEC 110.26 working space at PCS/disconnect.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Each cabinet needs its own (or a grouped) accessible disconnect near the unit; commissioning documentation is now a code item (ties to M&V/program commissioning).

site_constraints.title: Service capacity for charging: 125% continuous (80% loading) and NEC 220.87 existing-load method
site_constraints.rule: BESS charging is a continuous load: OCPDs/conductors sized at 125% of max rated charge current (i.e., standard breakers loaded <=80%). For existing services, NEC 220.87 allows using 12 months of recorded maximum demand (or a 30-day recording in some cases): 1.25 x max recorded demand + new load must not exceed service rating. EMS/PCS-limited charging can be counted at its setpoint (NEC 2023 EMS provisions, e.g., 220.70/750.30 - verify adopted edition).
site_constraints.formula: charge_headroom_kW = (service_amps * sqrt(3) * V_LL / 1000) - 1.25 * peak_12mo_kW ; allowed BESS charge kW <= headroom (or PCS-limited)

threshold.scope: continuous loading fraction of standard (non-100%-rated) OCPD

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Charging a 200 kW unit adds ~240 A at 480 V (~555 A at 208 V). Small 208 V retail services (400-800 A) often cannot absorb 200 kW of charging without a PCS charge cap; this, not fire code, can cap kW. Utilities may treat new charging kW as added load (load letter / service upgrade study) and may require import limits.

site_constraints.title: Outdoor groups above 600 kWh (IFC Table 1207.8 reading)
site_constraints.rule: Rooms/areas (and, per Mayfield's reading of IFC Table 1207.8, outdoor installations near exposures) containing Li-ion ESS shall not exceed 600 kWh aggregate. Exceeding it requires fire code official approval based on a Hazard Mitigation Analysis (1207.1.6) and large-scale fire testing (1207.1.7). Not applicable to dedicated-use buildings or remote outdoor installations.

threshold.scope: per fire area / outdoor group near exposures

site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Units per prescriptive group: 30/150 -> 4 units (600 kWh); 65/200 -> 3 units (600); 200/418 -> 1 unit (2 = 836 kWh exceeds); 200/600 -> 1 unit (exactly at limit). Larger clusters need HMA + LSFT approval, or split into separate groups separated per AHJ, or a remote outdoor location (>100 ft).

sku_impact.200kW/600kWh: max 1 per group (at limit); 2+ needs HMA+LSFT

site_constraints.applies_to: IFC 2021/2024 and NFPA 855-2023 jurisdictions. NFPA 855-2026 reportedly drops the separate max-stored-energy cap in favor of default HMA (low-confidence secondary source) - verify against adopted edition.

market_prices.notes: No primary 2026 C&I $/kWh found (Wood Mackenzie C&I pricing is paywalled). Secondary 2026 guides: typical C&I $280-580/kWh installed; small systems 50-500 kWh $500-1,000/kWh. NREL benchmark (standalone storage, battery $209/kWh): $380/kWh (4-h) to $895/kWh (0.5-h) - segment/vintage of that figure not confirmed. Wood Mackenzie reports utility-scale system pricing up ~23% Q4'24->Q4'25 (tariffs/FEOC). Expect $/kWh to rise as duration falls (200/418 > 200/600 > 30/150) and with tariff/FEOC-compliant cells. Use vendor quotes.

panel_notes.note: The most common way a BTM battery loses money is recharging into a new monthly peak (or a TOU on-peak demand window) right after shaving one. The dispatch model must enforce a site import ceiling during recharge (PCS import limit) and schedule charging in off-peak hours; a 200 kW unit recharging at full power adds 200 kW of demand.

On tariffs with demand ratchets (e.g., 80% of max over 11 months), one missed peak during a BMS fault, comms loss or maintenance sets the billing demand for a year. Model availability as a probability of losing a whole month's (or ratchet-year's) savings, not as a 3% energy haircut.

Deliverable kW for a program = min(rated kW, usable kWh / event hours). The 200/418 (2.1 h) cannot hold 200 kW for 3-h ConnectedSolutions or 4-h capacity events (~139 kW for 3 h, ~104 kW for 4 h before losses/DoD); the 30/150 (5 h) is energy-rich but kW-poor. Pick SKUs by the binding event duration in each market.

Non-export (32R/32F or PCS) means discharge kW <= site load minus import margin at that moment. Sites with peaky loads (HVAC-driven retail) can fully use 200 kW at peak but not at night; network-grid sites need larger margins. Use interval data minimum load in each dispatch window to cap the useful kW.

A 200 kW PCS at 208 V outputs ~555 A (~694 A at 125%), which almost never fits a load-side breaker; at 480 V it is ~241 A (~301 A). Screen each site's service voltage and switchboard ampacity first; 208 V sites usually need a step-up transformer, supply-side tap or PCS-limited output, all of which add cost.

Programs and VPP aggregation need revenue-grade interval metering (often a dedicated storage meter plus the utility billing meter), 1-15 min telemetry, and secure always-on comms. Budget cellular gateways, CT/PT upgrades and a utility meter change; lost telemetry during an event typically counts as non-performance.

panel_notes.topic: UL 9540A / LSFT is the real permit gate
panel_notes.note: Because every SKU exceeds the 50 kWh unit limit and the 418/600 kWh units hit the 600 kWh group cap alone, permitting depends on the vendor's UL 9540A (and increasingly large-scale fire test per NFPA 855-2026 Annex G.11 / UL 9540A Ed. 6, effective 2027-01-01) data. Get the full test report (not a summary letter) and tested spacing before signing site leases.

For construction beginning in 2026+, the storage MACR must be >=55% (rising to 75% by 2030) or the entire ITC is lost. Most low-cost LFP cabinets use Chinese cells/PCS; require supplier MACR certifications under Notice 2026-15 and price non-compliance risk into the model.

The <1 MW AC prevailing-wage exemption uses aggregate nameplate of facilities with integrated operations; five 200 kW cabinets at one site = 1.0 MW and lose the exemption (6% base without PWA). Cap per-site AC nameplate at <1,000 kW (e.g., four 200 kW + one 65 kW = 865 kW) or plan for PWA compliance.

Property insurers and host landlords increasingly require UL 9540 listing, 9540A/LSFT reports, NFPA 855 compliance, separation from the host building and remote monitoring; some impose larger setbacks than code. Confirm the host's carrier accepts the installation before design freeze.

Coastal/urban sites (NYC, Boston, CT shoreline, Chicago basements) must place cabinets and PCS above the design flood elevation; outdoor pads may need raised platforms, which change structural design, access and fire-department reach.

panel_notes.topic: Setbacks from egress, openings and air intakes
panel_notes.note: Beyond the code 10 ft from egress/lot lines/buildings, keep cabinets away from rooftop/wall HVAC intakes, operable windows and doors to avoid off-gas ingestion; AHJs often add these conditions during plan review.

418-600 kWh outdoor cabinets are multi-ton units needing crane access, engineered pads, bollards and fire-apparatus access; rooftop placement requires structural review and is rarely economic. Get vendor shipping weights and lift points early - they decide feasibility at tight urban sites.

HVAC/liquid-cooling fans run during charge/discharge and hot weather (including at night when charging). Check local property-line noise limits (e.g., state/municipal noise rules) for sites adjacent to residences; UL 9540 3rd ed. added noise-related requirements but local ordinances govern.

Auxiliary HVAC/heating loads are typically fed behind the customer meter and erode savings (and can add to demand); model them explicitly by climate. Warranties usually cap annual throughput/cycles, average SOC, C-rate and temperature - stacking daily arbitrage with DR and demand management can breach them; model a throughput budget.

open_questions: NFPA 855-2026: exact retained thresholds (20 kWh Li-ion, 50 kWh unit, 600 kWh area) vs. reported removal of the max-stored-energy cap - verify from the standard text; also which target states/AHJs have adopted 2026 (check MA 527 CMR 1, CT SFSC, NYC FC, IL OSFM, CA CFC 2025).

IFC elevation limit for electrochemical ESS (75 ft above fire department vehicle access / 30 ft below exit discharge) recalled from code structure but not confirmed in a search summary - verify in IFC 2021/2024 1207.5.3.
Whether the IFC 50 kWh unit limit and 600 kWh MAQ apply to outdoor walk-in vs. non-walk-in cabinets 'near exposures' is AHJ-interpreted; confirm with each AHJ and the vendor's 9540A report.
5-year MACRS retention for 48E energy storage after OBBBA: practitioner summaries conflict in wording - confirm with tax counsel/statute text (P.L. 119-21).
FEOC: confirm Notice 2026-15 safe-harbor tables status and specified-foreign-entity/foreign-influenced-entity effective dates for taxpayers.
Domestic content manufactured-products % for storage beginning construction in 2026 (50%) and after 2026 (55%) taken from 48E-general summaries - verify for energy storage technology.
C&I installed cost $/kWh for 2026 not available from a primary source (Wood Mackenzie C&I pricing paywalled; NREL Q1-2025 benchmark spreadsheet not opened) - use vendor quotes.
Aux load, degradation and availability values are low-confidence industry ranges - replace with per-SKU vendor data (aux kW vs ambient curve, warranty SOH curve, availability guarantee).
Utility-specific non-export settings (32R/32F pickup, delays, PCS OLRT 2 s vs 30 s, inadvertent export magnitude limits) vary - pull each utility's interconnection handbook (covered in state files).

NEC 2023 220.70/750.30 EMS load-calculation credit for PCS-limited charging - confirm section numbers and local adoption (MA 527 CMR 12 = NEC 2023 w/ amendments; NYC Electrical Code; CA CEC 2022 = NEC 2020).

assumptions.label: Usable AC energy fraction
assumptions.description: AC energy deliverable per kWh of product nameplate (depth of discharge × discharge losses). Set to 1.0 if the SKU kWh is already usable AC energy; PNNL’s LCOS convention uses 0.80.

assumptions.label: Round-trip efficiency (AC)

assumptions.label: Demand-shave capture factor

assumptions.description: Used when a program’s event duration is unknown; flagged on the stream.

assumptions.label: Peak-tag dispatch hours
assumptions.description: Hours the battery holds output around a forecast system peak.

assumptions.description: Non-export cap on discharge during events.

assumptions.label: TOU arbitrage capture
assumptions.description: Share of theoretical daily TOU spread captured.

assumptions.label: Demand-management cycling days
assumptions.description: Days per year the battery cycles for demand management (round-trip loss costing).
